## Background 

There are many *graphics systems* in R for making plots and figures. These include **"base R graphics"** like the `plot()` and add-on packages like **ggplot2**.

Let's compare how we make a simple graph with these two systems:

We can use the in-built `cars` dataset"

```{r}
head(cars)
```

A base R plot:

```{r}
plot(cars)
```

Now for **ggplot2**.

Before I can use ggplot2, I need to install it on my computer. To do this, we can use the function `install.packages("ggplot2")`

> **N.B.** We never run an `install.packages()` in our quarto doc (we run it in our R console) as it would re-install the package every time I render my document.

Once installed, we still need to load up the package into our R session. We do this with a `library()` call

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(cars)
```

Every ggplot needs at least 3 inputs:

- the **data** (a data.frame of the studd we want to plot)
- the **aesthetics** (how the data maps to the plot)
- the **geom** layer (how you want the plot drawn, points, lines, etc.)

```{r}
ggplot(cars) +
  aes(x=speed, y=dist) +
  geom_point()
```

## Let's add some features (more layers)

Let's add a trend line that shows the relationship between `speed` and `distance`:
```{r}
ggplot(cars) +
  aes(x=speed, y=dist) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_smooth()
```

```{r}
ggplot(cars) +
  aes(x=speed, y=dist) + 
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method="lm", se=FALSE) + 
  theme_bw() + 
  labs(x="Speed (MPH)", 
       y="Stopping Distance (ft)", 
       title="Stopping distance of some old cars")
```

## Gene Expression Plot

First we will read some expression data for the effect of a GLP-1 drug

```{r}
url <- "https://bioboot.github.io/bimm143_S20/class-material/up_down_expression.txt"
genes <- read.delim(url)
head(genes)
```
```{r}
ggplot(genes) + 
  aes(x=Condition1, y=Condition2) + 
  geom_point() + 
  theme_bw()
```

```{r}
ggplot(genes) + 
  aes(x=Condition1, y=Condition2, col=State) + 
  geom_point() + 
  theme_bw()
```

```{r}
ggplot(genes) + 
  aes(x=Condition1, y=Condition2, col=State) + 
  geom_point() + 
  theme_bw() + 
  scale_colour_manual(values=c("blue", "gray", "red")) + 
  labs(x="No Drug", y="Drug", title="GLP-1 inhibitor effects on gene expression")
```

Number of Genes
```{r}
nrow(genes)
```
Number of columns
```{r}
ncol(genes)
```

Column Names
```{r}
colnames(genes)
```

```{r}
table(genes$State) 
```

```{r}
n.total <- nrow(genes)
n.up <- sum(genes$State == "up")

round(n.up/n.total*100, 2)
```

## Going further

Here we read the famous *gapminder* dataset:

```{r}
url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jennybc/gapminder/master/inst/extdata/gapminder.tsv"

gapminder <- read.delim(url)
head(gapminder)
```

>Q. How many entries are in this dataset?

```{r}
nrow(gapminder)
```

>Q. How many different "country" values are in this dataset?

```{r}
unique(gapminder$country)
```


```{r}
length(unique(gapminder$country))
```

```{r}
table(gapminder$country)
```


Let's make our first plot of `gdpPercap` vs `lifeExp`:

```{r}
ggplot(gapminder) + 
  aes(x=gdpPercap, y=lifeExp) + 
  geom_point()
```

```{r}
ggplot(gapminder) + 
  aes(x=gdpPercap, y=lifeExp, col=continent) + 
  geom_point(alpha=0.2)
```


One useful layer we can add to explore big datasets like this is called "facetting"

```{r}
ggplot(gapminder) + 
  aes(x=gdpPercap, y=lifeExp, col=continent) + 
  geom_point(alpha=0.2) + 
  facet_wrap(~continent)
```

### Limit to 1977 and 2007 

We can install and use the **dplyr** package to help "filter" the full dataset down to a smaller subset that only includes the years we want.

First, we need to run `install.packages("dplyr")` and load it with `library(dplyr)`.

```{r}
library(dplyr)

filter(gapminder, year==2007, country=="Canada")
filter(gapminder, year==1977, country=="Canada")
```

>Q. Make a histogram of lifeExp

```{r}
ggplot(gapminder) + 
  aes(lifeExp, fill=continent) + 
  geom_histogram()
```

Boxplot
```{r}
ggplot(gapminder) + 
  aes(lifeExp, fill=continent) + 
  geom_boxplot()
```
